source: every COBJ record across 102 plugins in load order, and the records their CNAM and BNAM point at
readFrom: BNAM is the workbench keyword, CNAM is the output item, NAM1 is how many it makes, COCT and CNTO are the inputs, CTDA is the conditions, which are in every row's needs list
event: mp.onCraft(actorFormId, craftedItemBaseId, count, recipeId). All four arguments are numbers. The keys of this table are desc strings, so look a row up with RECIPES_BY_ID[mp.getDescFromId(recipeId)] and never with recipeId itself, which matches nothing. Returning false refuses the craft outright: CraftEvent::OnFireSuccess is what removes the inputs and adds the output, and GameModeEvent::Fire only calls it when nobody blocked.
key: the recipe's form id in lower case hex, a colon, and the file it belongs to. mp.getDescFromId turns onCraft's fourth argument into one.
rank: which of classes.md's four ranks the row asks for: novice, advanced, expert or master. Ranked by WHAT ITS INPUTS COST A PRODUCER, taking the dearest thing it asks for, because that is the rung somebody has to have reached before they could gather the makings at all. Where part of the list is produced by nobody, that dearest placed input is a FLOOR and not the answer: it can raise the row above what the output sells for and never lower it, because an item nothing produces is an unknown cost rather than a free one. A row whose inputs no class produces at all falls back to what the output sells for, ranked inside its own half. rankFrom says which of the three answered. classes.md sets no numbers for any of this and nothing in the game records ranks a recipe, so every judgement is a knob at the top of the script: RANK_FROM_INPUT_COST, PRODUCER_TABLES, SERVER_PRODUCERS, PRODUCER_RANK_IS_LOWEST, INPUT_RANK_IS_THE_DEAREST, UNPLACED_INPUT_RULE, RANK_SHARE and SECOND_RULE_KEY.
inputItems: every CNTO the record carried: what the recipe wants, how many, and which class produces that item at which rank. producedBy is the class that gets it at the LOWEST rank, because that is what the thing costs to get hold of; alsoProducedBy, where it is present, is every OTHER class that produces the same item, at the rank that class produces it at, whether that is higher than producedAt or exactly level with it. A tied class was dropped from this field until 21 September, which made the farmer invisible for wheat in every consumer of this file. producedBy null means nothing in this repository hands that item over: no table in this folder and no verb in game\gamemode.js. Read out of the recipe's own CNTO subrecords, eight bytes each, a form id then a count.
suppliedBy: on each input beside producedBy, and a different question: producedBy is the class that digs it out of the ground, and suppliedBy is the class the input rests on however many benches away it is. Steel Ingot reads producedBy null and suppliedBy miner, because a smelter row makes it out of ore. hops is how many recipes stand between the class and the input, 0 for handed straight over and 1 for a smelter or a tanning rack away, and suppliedVia names the recipe of the last of those steps. suppliedBy null means nothing in this world supplies it at all, directly or through any bench: it is bought, looted or dropped. What ranks a row is suppliedAt and not producedAt.
theHop: how suppliedBy is worked out. An input that is itself the output of a recipe costs what that recipe's dearest input costs, taken over all 5116 recipes and not just the 3437 with an owner, because the smelter and the tanning rack are among the 1679 nobody owns. It is a fixpoint: every item starts unknown, every recipe is asked again each round, and a cost only ever moves from unknown to a rank or from a rank to a cheaper one, so it settles, and it settles in three rounds on this build. A recipe says nothing about its output while any part of its own list is unknown, for the reason written at UNPLACED_INPUT_RULE. A row that turns a finished good back into stock, a fur hood into a Steel Ingot, is a refund and not a source and sets nothing; 1072 rows have that shape.
inputsWithNoProducer: how many of the row's inputs nothing in this repository produces. Read it with inputRank: "the dearest input is novice" means one thing on a row where that is the whole list and another on a row with four unknowns beside it, and not reading it is how a 3100 gold dragonbone plate went out at novice on 21 September off one novice hunter's fox pelt.
rankFrom: which rule gave this row its rank: what its inputs cost a producer, what it sells for, or the second rule named in SECOND_RULE_KEY. The second rule is used for one half at a time and only where the first two leave a rung with nothing on it, and every use of it is printed by name when the table is built.
rankByValue: what the old rule would have said: the rank this row got from the price of what it makes, inside its own half. Kept on every row so the two answers can be compared rather than one of them quietly replacing the other.
inputRank: the rank of the dearest input this row asks for, and inputRankWho is the class that produces it. Null when nothing it asks for is produced by any class.
crossTier: scripts\dev\Check-Balance.ps1 reads inputRank against rank and reports every half by how far its recipes sit from what their inputs cost, and reads alsoProducedBy to report every row ranked below a class that has to climb higher for something on its list. That is the imbalance Patrick asked about on 21 September, stated as a number. Both scripts print it; neither fails on it, because which of the two ladders should move is a decision.
rungsNobodyCanGatherFor: on a half: a rung that holds recipes and not one of them can be gathered for at that rank, which is an empty rung wearing a label and is what the second rule can leave behind. Build-RecipeTable.ps1 fails the build for any half that has one and is not named in its HALVES_WITH_AN_UNSTANDABLE_RUNG knob with the measured reason, so a half carrying this field is one somebody decided to live with and wrote down.
rankedByInputCost: on each half: how many of its rows the input cost rule could answer for and how many fell back to price, counted BEFORE any second rule ran. Where the half also carries a secondRule field, that rule then re-ranked every row of it, so read rankFrom on the row for what actually decided it.
family: what kind of thing the row makes, which is how the recipe book in the K panel groups a half's work. Read off the output record and nothing else: a keyword that names a kind, which is a weapon type keyword, one of the five armour slot keywords, a clothing slot keyword or a Gourmet food type keyword. An output carrying exactly one of those takes its name from it. An output carrying two names neither, because the Cloaks&Capes cloaks carry a helmet or cuirass slot beside a necklace slot and a cloak is none of those, so two kinds falls through with no kind at all to the record's own type: AMMO is arrows and bolts, ARMO is other armour and clothing, and so on. familyFrom on every row says which of the three readings answered. classes.md sets none of this and names no families at all, so the groups and their words are knobs at the top of the script: FAMILY_ARMOR_SLOTS, FAMILY_KEYWORD_PREFIXES, FAMILY_KEYWORD_NOT, FAMILY_NAMES, FAMILY_BY_TYPE, FAMILY_OTHERWISE and FAMILY_SHARE_TO_WARN.
sisterHalf: classes.md gives you the novice work of the other half of your own profession for nothing, and no further than novice. The gate can answer that because every row carries a rank.
needs: the recipe's own conditions, read out of its CTDA subrecords. An empty list means anybody standing at the bench can make it. serverSees false means the fork has no function for that condition and the server answers True, so the only thing enforcing it is the crafting menu on the machine in front of the person, which hides the recipe rather than refusing it.
default: a recipe id this table does not carry is one nobody owns, and anybody may make it
fires: false means the server is never asked about this recipe. CraftService::RecipeItemsMatch throws out the armour table (adb78) and the sharpening wheel (88108) before it considers anything, so tempering never reaches onCraft.

Warrior.why: warriors do not craft. classes.md gives Bulwark and Berserker combat maneuvers rather than recipes, so there is nothing in the records to find and nothing for a crafting gate to refuse. The profession is offered like any other.

Mage.why: a mage has no halves. classes.md gives the Mage two schools and two starting spells, and none of it is a crafting recipe. What a mage knows is written by scripts\dev\Build-SpellTable.ps1.

Warrior/Bulwark.why: warriors do not craft. Bulwark and Berserker are halves of how somebody fights, and classes.md gives them combat maneuvers rather than recipes. There is nothing in the records to find.

Warrior/Berserker.why: the same. Warrior is the one profession whose halves are not about making anything.

Alchemist/Blightbrewer.why: Skyrim has no alchemy recipes. Not one COBJ record in the whole load order names an alchemy bench keyword: potions are worked out from the effects that the ingredients share, in the alchemy menu, and no record is involved. The poison bit that would split this half from the Physicker is proved and ready in the code above, so the moment a mod adds an alchemy bench recipe it lands here by itself. The Physicker's poultice and remedy (#1383) are named recipes in RECIPE_OWNER, not brews, so they are not this half's.

Cook/Confectioner.movedOneRung: 8 row(s) moved one rung each to fill an empty rung, HOLE_FILL_MOVES_ONE_RUNG: MAG_RecipeFoodSweetRoll (Sweet Roll), advanced to novice; MAG_RecipeFoodJazbayDumpling (Jazbay Dumpling), advanced to novice; MAG_RecipeFoodSnowberryDumpling (Snowberry Dumpling), advanced to novice; MAG_RecipeFoodJuniperDumpling (Juniper Berry Dumpling), advanced to novice; MAG_RecipeFoodBoiledCremeTreat (Boiled Creme Treat), advanced to novice; MAG_RecipeFoodHoneyNutTreat (Honey Nut Treat), advanced to novice; MAG_RecipeFoodJellyDumpling (Jelly Dumpling), advanced to novice; MAG_UpgradeRecipeFoodBoiledCremeTreat (Boiled Creme Treat), advanced to novice
Cook/Confectioner.rungsNobodyCanGatherFor: the novice rung holds 8 row(s) and not one of them can be gathered for below advanced; the nearest is Sweet Roll, wanting advanced work from a farmer
Cook/Confectioner.andThatIsAllowedBecause: every one of its 28 rows wants a Sack of Flour and a pat of Butter, counted over the whole half on 21 September, and flour is made from Wheat, which harvests.json ranks advanced for a gatherer and for a farmer alike. So the cheapest thing a Confectioner can bake is advanced work to gather for and the novice rung cannot be stood on whatever rule ranks the half: by input cost all 28 land 20 advanced and 8 expert and none novice (28 September), and filling the empty novice rung (HOLE_FILL_MOVES_ONE_RUNG) only relabels eight of the advanced ones. This appeared the day the hop was followed and it was always true; before it, flour had no producer at all and every row read as costing nothing. It closes when somebody decides where a Confectioner's flour comes from, which is the same decision HALVES_NOBODY_CAN_START is already waiting on for this half: all 28 rows are behind two vanilla perks nobody here will ever hold, so nothing is being opened to anybody at any rank yet.
Cook/Confectioner.nothingToMakeOnDayOne: every one of its 28 recipes carries two vanilla perk conditions, function index 448: MAG_FoodUpgradePerk03 out of Gourmet.esp on all 28, and a second perk named for the recipe itself, MAG_RecipePerkSnowberryDumpling and its like, on all 28 as well. classes.md says no perk menu opens and vanilla progression is off, so nobody here will ever hold either. The server would wave the condition through, because the fork has no function for that index, but Skyrim's own crafting menu evaluates it first and never lists the recipe, so onCraft is not even reached. The dessert keyword split is right and the half is real; what is missing is somebody deciding what a new Confectioner starts able to bake. Four of the 28 want an item on top of the perks.

Enchanter/Bladebinder.rungsNobodyCanGatherFor: the novice rung holds 3 row(s) and not one of them can be gathered for below master; the nearest is Staff of Flames, wanting master work from a miner. the advanced rung holds 6 row(s) and not one of them can be gathered for below master; the nearest is Staff of Lightning Bolts, wanting master work from a miner. the expert rung holds 4 row(s) and not one of them can be gathered for below master; the nearest is Staff of Icy Spear, wanting master work from a miner
Enchanter/Bladebinder.andThatIsAllowedBecause: all of its 161 rows but the Aetherial Staff want a Heart Stone, which is master mining (the miner page, issues #1380 and #1586, RANK_BY_ORE in Build-OreTable.ps1), so by input cost all 160 land on master. Patrick, 4 October (#1622): each college book staff at its spell's rank, named in RECIPE_RANK. So the thirteen the Bladebinder page keeps sit novice 3, advanced 6 and expert 4, and the other 148, all cut, stay on master. The novice, advanced and expert rungs hold only staves whose stone nobody below master can dig, so a Bladebinder below master buys heart stones from a master miner. That is the decision, not a hole: the recipe says what the spell gate already says, because a staff is not made until its spell is on you and a Bladebinder unlocks a spell on K only at a rank at least the spell's.

Enchanter/Wardweaver.why: the only enchanting recipes in the build are the staff recipes on the Dragonborn staff enchanter, and a staff is a weapon, so they all land on the Bladebinder. Enchanting a cuirass or a robe is the enchanting menu and not a record, so the Wardweaver has nothing to own here.

Tailor/Liverywright.movedOneRung: 6 row(s) moved one rung each to fill an empty rung, HOLE_FILL_MOVES_ONE_RUNG: IARImperialKnightCape (Imperial Knight Cape), master to expert; IARDwarvenMageUnarmoredRobe (Dwarven Mage Unarmored Robe), master to expert; IARShamanURobe (Shaman Unarmored Robe), master to expert; IARTribunalUnarmoredRobeBlack (Tribunal Unarmored Robe Black), master to expert; IARTribunalUnarmoredRobeBlue (Tribunal Unarmored Robe Blue), master to expert; IARTribunalUnarmoredRobeGreen (Tribunal Unarmored Robe Green), master to expert

6aa09:Hothtrooper44_ArmorCompilation.esp.whyThatRank: what it makes is worth 125 gold, which puts it in the master share of what this half makes. Then moved one rung, master to expert, because the expert rung of this half was empty with work above it (HOLE_FILL_MOVES_ONE_RUNG)
